subject.title: fix(cli): reject unknown models in config set

question: Should `openclaw config set` intentionally reject changed text-model references that cannot resolve in the current provider/catalog and auth-profile context, instead of persisting them for a later agent-run failure?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility boundary change affecting existing CLI automation and provider/auth-dependent configuration, so correctness evidence alone cannot choose the product contract.

options.title: Accept set-time validation
options.body: Merge the runtime-aligned fail-closed behavior so invalid changed text-model references are rejected before configuration is persisted.

options.title: Preserve deferred persistence
options.body: Keep the historical write behavior and pursue an explicitly opt-in validation path if maintainers do not want existing automation to fail earlier.

recommendation.title: Accept set-time validation
recommendation.body: Merge the runtime-aligned fail-closed behavior so invalid changed text-model references are rejected before configuration is persisted.

likelyOwner.reason: The recorded member comment explicitly identifies this compatibility acceptance as the remaining human decision.
